findings.title: VIEW permission on all groups grants global group manage
findings.body: canManage() with no group argument returns true for either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. This method backs GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup via requireManage(), so an FGAP admin granted only view access to all groups can create top-level groups and perform other global manage operations. Unlike canManage(GroupModel), which correctly requires only MANAGE, the global check should require MANAGE only.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: Group authorization resources are created with the group ID as the resource name, while Resource.getId() is an unrelated internal authorization-store UUID. This loop calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), which does findByName(server, UUID) and therefore misses the per-group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and then adds that same UUID to the granted set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount expect actual GroupModel IDs in UserModel.GROUPS, so per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are not correctly used to filter or count group members. It should pass and return groupResource.getName() and must not treat the all-groups type resource (named 'Groups') as a group.

findings.title: Existing FGAP v2 realms never receive the new Groups resource or scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately whenever the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change therefore keep a resource server containing only the previously defined Clients and Users all-type resources and scopes, with no Groups resource and no manage-members/view-members/manage-membership scopes. Group permissions cannot be created or evaluated correctly in such realms; GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission can also receive null from getResourceTypeResource and pass it to policyStore.findByResource. The schema initialization needs an upgrade path that adds missing resource types and scopes for an existing admin-permissions client, or evaluation needs null-safe handling.
